title: 3.3.16 Lab: lastItem(items)
description: Write lastItem(items): read the last item of an array parameter and return it, leaving the array exactly as it was. Practice, not graded: the checks call your function.

steps.title: Write lastItem
steps.instructions: Write a function declaration called lastItem that takes one parameter, items, the array to look at.

steps.title: Read the last item
steps.instructions: The last index is one less than the length (3.3.2), so the last item is items[items.length - 1].

steps.title: Return it and leave the array alone
steps.instructions: Return that item with return. Do not use .pop(): it also gives back the last item, but it removes it from the array, and a function that only looks at an array must leave it as it found it (3.3.15).

steps.title: Check both
steps.instructions: Call lastItem on an array, then console.log the result and the array, to show the array still has every item.

requirements.title: lastItem is defined with one parameter
requirements.description: Code defines a function named lastItem with exactly one parameter. Help: 3.3.15 (Arrays and Functions)
requirements.hint: Write function lastItem(items) { ... } with exactly that name and one name between the parentheses.

requirements.title: lastItem hands back a value with return
requirements.description: lastItem contains a return statement. Help: 3.2.11 (Getting a Value Back with `return`)
requirements.hint: The answer must leave the function with return, not console.log.

requirements.title: lastItem returns the last item and leaves the array alone
requirements.description: lastItem(items) gives back the last item of the array, and the array you pass in is not changed. Help: 3.3.15 (Arrays and Functions)
requirements.hint: lastItem must give back the last item and leave the array as it was. items[items.length - 1] reads the last item. items[items.length] is one place too far (undefined), items[0] is the first item, and items.pop() removes the item from the array.
